reader.requirement: At --std 85, a Procedure Division reference to LINE-COUNTER must be qualified by a report-name when the program has more than one report (an unqualified one is refused; with one report it resolves), and in the Report Section an unqualified LINE-COUNTER means the enclosing report's counter while another report's counter must be qualified by that report's name (report-name is the highest qualifier, XIII.3.5.3 SR3).
reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|DialectLevel|Has(' over CounterResolver.cs: the only edition test is LinageFileOf's Has(2014) (LINAGE-COUNTER, another rule); ReportOf and CounterExpr consult none. ReservedWords.Table.cs row LINE-COUNTER is reserved at all four editions (identical, no switch). No ConstructRegistry/VersionConformancePass entry for the counter reference. RD GLOBAL (the only thing that widens NearestInScope) is not in the 1985 RD format (XIII.3.5.2), so the 1985 path is the latest edition's code.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1456_other_report_counters_85 covers the Report Section half (implicit qualification and explicit qualification of another report's counter); the Procedure Division refusal of an unqualified counter with two reports, the single-report unqualified case, and a non-report qualifier are not exercised

reader.notes: ReportOf is the one resolver both directions use: an OF/IN qualifier must name a report, an unqualified reference inside an RD takes the enclosing report, otherwise exactly one report must be visible. Every probe matched the 1985 text. At --std 85 the diagnostic cites §2023:8.4.2.2.3 SR9 instead of the 1985 rule; only the wording is affected.
reader.at-2023: same code path, no edition arm

refuter.evidence: The reader's premise that RD GLOBAL is not in 1985 is false: the IPC module's RD format has [IS GLOBAL] (OK §1985:X.4.4.2 'RD report-name-1 IS GLOBAL CODE literal-1') and makes the counters global names (OK §1985:X.4.4.4 GR1 'the special registers LINE-COUNTER and PAGE-COUNTER are global names'). So I attacked the global path the reader skipped, through CounterResolver.ReportOf's NearestInScope arm, at --std 85 (run_case.py, refute-1985-078/): lcglob1 (container RD R1 IS GLOBAL, contained program with no RD, unqualified LINE-COUNTER) exit 0, 'INNER 02': resolves to the one accessible counter. lcglob2 (two GLOBAL RDs, contained program with no RD, unqualified) gives COBOL2729 'unqualified LINE-COUNTER with more than one report description entry', exit 65. lcnong1 (one non-GLOBAL RD in the container, contained program unqualified) gives COBOL2729 'the program has no report description entry', exit 65: a local counter is not visible. lcnongq (LINE-COUNTER OF R1 in the contained program, R1 not GLOBAL) gives COBOL2729 'the qualifier shall name a report description entry', exit 65: a qualifier that is not accessible is refused. lcglobq (R1 GLOBAL, LINE-COUNTER OF R1 in a contained program that has its own R3) exit 0, 'INNER 02'. lcgloby (two GLOBAL RDs plus the contained program's own R3, unqualified) exit 0, 'INNER 00' (R3's counter). That follows §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR3a (OK: 'If the name is declared in program B, the object in program B is the referenced object'), reading 'more than one LINE-COUNTER exists in a program' as the counters the X.1.3.8.2 resolution leaves. Every probe matched OK §1985:XIII.3.5.6 SR3 'must be qualified by a report-name whenever it is referenced in the Procedure Division'.
